title: fix: coalesce comm_msg state updates within a flush cycle
description:
## Summary

Fixes #212 — ipyleaflet LayersControl losing track of layers when reactive effects do remove+add within a single flush cycle.

**Root cause:** When multiple reactive effects modify the same widget (e.g., `map.remove(old_layer)` then `map.add(new_layer)`), each trait change sends a separate `comm_msg` to the client. The intermediate states (e.g., "layers after remove but before add") cause race conditions in ipyleaflet's async JS layer management. The final map rendering was correct, but the LayersControl overlay list would lose entries.

**Fix:** State-update `comm_msg` messages (`method="update"`) for the same model are now merged within each flush cycle, sending only the final value of each changed trait. This is equivalent to wrapping every reactive effect in ipywidgets' `hold_sync()`, but applied automatically at the transport layer. Non-update messages (`method="custom"`) are still sent individually.

**Key changes:**
- `_comm.py`: Added coalescing logic in `_publish_msg` — first update for a `comm_id` registers an `on_flushed` callback; subsequent updates merge their state dict into the pending entry
- Buffer paths for overridden state keys are properly replaced during merges
- `comm_close` and non-update `comm_msg` messages are unaffected

## Test plan

- [x] 5 new unit tests covering: basic coalescing, cross-trait merging, buffer handling, non-update passthrough, independent coalescing per model
- [x] New Playwright test (`ipyleaflet_layer_update`) that verifies LayersControl stays consistent after remove+add cycles
- [x] All 90 unit tests pass
- [x] All existing Playwright tests pass (marker click, geojson hover, rerender cleanup)
- [x] `make check` passes (format + types + unit tests)

title: Require `ipywidgets>8.0`; upgrade `@jupyter-widgets/html-manager`
description:
## Why

With ipywidgets 8, widgets nested inside other widgets didn't work reliably in Shiny. Some didn't render at all, such as a Plotly `FigureWidget` or a styled `HTML` widget inside an ipyleaflet popup. Others rendered but logged errors like `Class HTMLStyleModel not found in module @jupyter-widgets/controls@2.0.0`: ipyleaflet popups, `WidgetControl` children, leafmap legends (100+ errors from its toolbar), and `output_widget()` inside `@render.ui`. Separately, ipyleaflet maps with many markers turned gray on every re-render.

The cause was that shinywidgets still bundled `@jupyter-widgets/html-manager` 0.20, the ipywidgets 7-era manager, which doesn't know the ipywidgets 8 model classes. This PR moves to 1.0.14 (the ipywidgets 8 line) and fixes the Shiny-specific issues the new manager exposed.

Fixes #75
Fixes #101
Fixes #137
Fixes #157
Fixes #215

It also fixes the Plotly-child part of #194; the spinner part of that issue is unrelated.

## ⚠️ Breaking change: ipywidgets 8 is now required

The minimum is now `ipywidgets>=8.0.0`. ipywidgets 8 has been out since 2022, and supporting 7 alongside the new manager would mean keeping compatibility shims for both.

Older widget packages built for ipywidgets 7 still work. ipyleaflet 0.17.3 on ipywidgets 8.1.8 handled popups, viewport resizes, and repeated re-renders without errors.

## Other user-visible fixes

- **Fonts in widget CSS load.** FontAwesome and other fonts in the bundled widget CSS were requested from `/@jupyter-widgets/<hash>.woff2` and returned 404. They now resolve from the package's static directory.
- **Clearing widgets doesn't hang.** When a widget is torn down while its child models are still loading, the pending lookups are cancelled right away instead of waiting out a timeout.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Out-of-order comm messages** (`js/src/output.ts`). Shiny delivers `comm_open` messages one by one, so a parent's state can reference a child model that hasn't been registered yet. The base manager rejects that case. `OutputManager.get_model()` now waits for the child to arrive, gives up after 30s, and cancels any pending waits when `clear_state()` runs.
  - Trade-off: when a model will *never* arrive, the error now appears after 30s instead of immediately. This happens with #108 (`register_widget()` inside `render.ui`) and #245 (widgets created at import time). Both are broken on `main` too.
- **Font path fix** (`shinywidgets/static/require-config.js`). It maps the `@jupyter-widgets/*` AMD module IDs to the real script directory. It has to load before `libembed-amd.js`; the comment in the file explains why.
- **Fill CSS.** `.forward-fill-potential > *` is now `> .lm-Widget`, so that temporary sibling elements such as tooltips don't get sized as fill items.
- Most of the diff is regenerated output: `libembed-amd.js`, the font assets, and `yarn.lock`. `js/src/_input.ts` was unused, since webpack only bundles `output.ts`, and is removed.

## Testing

- `make check` passes: format, Pyright, and 89 unit tests.
- The Playwright suite passes in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. New regression tests cover popup HTML children (including viewport resize), GeoJSON hover → `WidgetControl` updates, dynamically inserted widget outputs, and cleanup while model lookups are still pending.
- **Issue triage.** I reproduced about 35 open issues on `main` and on this branch (with #246 stacked on top), using a scripted headless browser to check console errors and rendered content. Each issue listed under "Fixes" fails on `main` and passes here; #215 was also checked on this branch alone. No repro broke that works on `main`, and this branch logged no console errors that `main` didn't.
- Checked manually: a broad core and third-party widget gallery, a 1,000-marker map, font delivery, and two Shinylive exports.
- Not covered: the exact `ipywidgets==8.0.0` floor (runtime tests used 8.1.8) and a full WebSocket reconnect.

title: fix: Plotly jump on rerender in filling layouts
description:
Closes #208.

Plotly `FigureWidget` can perform an initial draw at its internal fallback height before resizing to the actual container height. In filling layouts, that allows the output to become visible at the wrong height and then visibly jump to the final size.

This PR fixes that by delaying reveal for Plotly outputs until Plotly's own resize cycle has completed.

## What changed

- Keep the existing widget implementation flow for non-Plotly widgets.
- Pass `widget_pkg` from the server render payload so the client does not need to infer whether a widget is Plotly.
- Add a small Plotly-specific helper module in `js/src/plotly.ts`.
- For Plotly outputs:
  - keep the output hidden,
  - wait for Plotly's initial render/afterplot cycle,
  - call `Plotly.Plots.resize(...)` directly on the graph div,
  - wait for the post-resize `plotly_afterplot`,
  - then reveal the output.

## Reviewer context

This is intentionally narrow. It is not a general refactor of widget readiness logic.

The bug is tied to Plotly's render sequence:
1. initial draw at fallback height,
2. `plotlywidget-after-render`,
3. resize,
4. repaint at the real container height.

The fix is to avoid revealing the widget between steps 1 and 4.

## Test coverage

- Add a self-contained Playwright regression that reproduces the Plotly reveal/resize issue without depending on `examples/plotly/app.py` or extra Python packages.
- Keep the existing Plotly rerender cleanup coverage.
- Add a unit test covering the new `widget_pkg` render payload field.

## Verification

title: Bulk restore: replace per-widget comm_open with single manager state message
description:
## Summary

Replaces the per-widget `comm_open` initialization pattern with a single bulk `shinywidgets_manager_state` message per render output. This eliminates widget model registration races and reduces message count from O(N) to O(1) for complex widget trees.

## Problem

When rendering a widget with many children (e.g., an ipyleaflet `Map` with 50+ `Marker` layers), each widget in the dependency graph sends its own `comm_open` message to the browser. The client-side `handle_comm_open` is async — it loads the widget's JS module, then calls `new_model()` to register the model. If `renderValue` arrives before all child models are fully registered, the parent widget's deserialization fails with "widget model not found" errors because it tries to resolve `IPY_MODEL_<id>` references to children that don't exist yet.

The root cause is that model registration happens asynchronously on a per-widget basis, with no guarantee that all models in a dependency graph are registered before any of them begin deserializing cross-references.

## Solution

### Server side (Python)

**New module: `shinywidgets/_bulk_state.py`**

- `find_ipy_model_refs(state)` — Recursively walks a serialized widget state dict and extracts all `IPY_MODEL_<id>` references. Used to discover the full dependency graph.
- `build_manager_state(root_widget, widget_instance_map, remove_buffers, collect_deps)` — BFS traversal from a root widget through its dependency graph. For each widget: calls `_repr_mimebundle_()` (needed for plotly), serializes state via `get_state()`, base64-encodes binary buffers, and collects HTML dependencies (deduplicated by name+version). Returns a payload containing the full widget closure.
- `materialize_bulk_comms(state_entries, widget_instance_map, comm_manager, comm_class, widget_comm_patch)` — Creates `ShinyComm(emit_open=False)` for each widget in the bulk closure, registering them in the comm manager without sending individual `comm_open` messages. Sets `_shinywidgets_bulk_owned = True` on each widget.

**Modified: `shinywidgets/_comm.py`**

- `ShinyComm.__init__` gains an `emit_open: bool = True` parameter. When `False`, the comm is registered in the manager and marked as not-closed, but no `comm_open` message is scheduled. This is used by `materialize_bulk_comms` — the client will receive the widget state through the bulk message instead.

**Modified: `shinywidgets/_shinywidgets.py`**

- `_open_shiny_comm` (the per-widget reactive effect at priority 99999) now checks `getattr(w, "_shinywidgets_bulk_owned", False)` at the top. If the bulk path already claimed the widget, the effect self-destructs without sending a `comm_open`.

**Modified: `shinywidgets/_render_widget_base.py`**

- `_render()` now calls `await self._send_bulk_state(widget, session)` before returning the render result.
- `_send_bulk_state()` orchestrates the bulk path: builds the full dependency closure via `build_manager_state`, materializes comms via `materialize_bulk_comms`, serializes the payload, and sends it as a `shinywidgets_manager_state` custom message.

### Client side (TypeScript)

**Modified: `js/src/output.ts`**

- New `restoreManagerState(mgr, state)` function: iterates over all models in the bulk state payload, decodes base64 buffers (using `put_buffers` from `@jupyter-widgets/base`), creates a `ShinyComm` for each, and calls `mgr.new_model()`. The key correctness property: `new_model()` calls `register_model()` **synchronously before its first `await`**, so all model promises are registered in `manager._models` before any async deserialization begins. This means cross-model `IPY_MODEL_` references always resolve, regardless of iteration order.
- New `shinywidgets_manager_state` custom message handler: renders HTML deps first (so widget JS modules are loadable), then calls `restoreManagerState`.
- Existing `shinywidgets_comm_open` handler now uses an `openQueue` promise chain to serialize processing. This hardens the legacy path for widgets not handled by bulk restore (e.g., dynamically created widgets after initial render).

### Activation logic

The bulk path only activates when the root widget's comm is still an `OrphanedShinyComm` at render time. This happens when widgets are constructed **inside** `@render_widget` — the common pattern for complex widget trees:

```python
@render_widget
def my_map():
    m = Map(center=(51.47, -0.00), zoom=12)
    for loc in locations:
        m.add_layer(Marker(location=loc))
    return m
```

When widgets are constructed **outside** `@render_widget` (e.g., at server function scope), Shiny's reactive effects phase runs `_open_shiny_comm` before the output renders. By the time `_render()` executes, the widget already has a live comm, and `_send_bulk_state` returns early to avoid duplicate model registration on the client.

## Message flow comparison

**Before (per-widget):**
```
Server → Client: comm_open (widget 1)    ← via on_flush
Server → Client: comm_open (widget 2)    ← via on_flush  
Server → Client: comm_open (widget N)    ← via on_flush
Server → Client: renderValue {model_id}  ← flush batch
Client: handle_comm_open(1) → async load JS → new_model(1) → async deserialize
Client: handle_comm_open(2) → async load JS → new_model(2) → async deserialize  
Client: renderValue → get_model(root) → deserialize → resolve IPY_MODEL refs → 💥 race
```

**After (bulk restore):**
```
Server → Client: shinywidgets_manager_state {all models}  ← send_custom_message
Server → Client: renderValue {model_id}                   ← flush batch
Client: restoreManagerState → new_model(1), new_model(2), ..., new_model(N)
          ↑ all promises registered synchronously before any deserialization
Client: await Promise.all(modelPromises) → all models resolve
Client: renderValue → get_model(root) → ✅ all refs available
```

## Test plan

- [x] 19 new unit tests across `test_bulk_state.py` and `test_comm_transport.py` covering:
  - `find_ipy_model_refs`: empty state, flat refs, nested dicts, lists, mixed nesting, dedup, non-model strings
  - `build_manager_state`: single widget, child traversal, deep graphs, buffer encoding, dep dedup, missing refs, `_repr_mimebundle_` invocation
  - `materialize_bulk_comms`: comm creation + flag setting, missing widget handling
  - `_open_shiny_comm` bulk-owned guard
  - `ShinyComm(emit_open=False)`: registration without scheduling, send/close still work
- [x] All 104 existing unit tests pass
- [x] Pyright type checking passes (0 errors)
- [x] Ruff format/lint passes
- [x] All 7 Playwright integration tests pass (altair, bokeh, plotly rerender cleanup; ipyleaflet marker click + rerender; buffer transport round-trip; isolate context rendering)

title: Fix browser-to-server widget buffer decoding
description:
## Summary
- decode inbound browser-to-server widget `buffers` on the Shiny side before forwarding comm messages to ipywidgets
- add a minimal `anywidget` Playwright regression that exercises both binary trait updates and binary custom messages

Closes #151.

## Problem
`shinywidgets` already base64-encodes browser-originated widget buffers so they can cross Shiny's input transport. The missing piece was on the server side: we were doing `json.loads()` and forwarding the message directly to the widget comm, which left `msg["buffers"]` as base64 strings. `ipywidgets.Widget._handle_msg()` expects bytes-like buffers for both:

- `update` messages, where `buffer_paths` are used to reconstruct binary state
- `custom` messages, where buffers are passed through to `on_msg` callbacks

As a result, browser-originated binary state/custom traffic was not protocol-correct even though the browser transport layer was already trying to preserve buffers.

## Test Coverage
This PR adds a small `anywidget`-based Playwright regression so the test isolates the browser-to-server binary transport behavior directly.

## What This PR Changes
### 1. Decode inbound buffers on the server
In `shinywidgets/_shinywidgets.py`, messages coming from `session.input.shinywidgets_comm_send()` now pass through a small `_decode_comm_buffers()` helper before `comm.handle_msg(msg)`.

That helper:
- leaves messages without buffers unchanged
- base64-decodes string buffers
- wraps decoded buffers in `memoryview`, which is accepted by ipywidgets' existing buffer handling
- leaves non-string buffers untouched if they ever appear

### 2. Add browser-to-server buffer regression coverage
`tests/playwright/buffer_transport/` adds a self-contained `anywidget` app and Playwright test that exercises both paths:

- normal synced trait update carrying binary state
- custom message carrying binary buffers

The server side reports the received payloads via Shiny text outputs so the test can assert the actual Python-visible state.

## Important Protocol Nuance Captured By The Test
The regression intentionally checks two different behaviors:

1. **Trait update path (`model.set(...); model.save_changes()`)**
   Even though the widget view creates a sliced `DataView`, upstream ipywidgets frontend logic collapses `ArrayBufferView` values to their full backing `ArrayBuffer` during normal state-sync serialization. So the correct observed value here is the full backing buffer: `00000UPDATE000` (`14 bytes`).

2. **Custom message path (`model.send(..., buffers=[...])`)**
   This path preserves the explicitly supplied sliced `Uint8Array`, so the correct observed value is just `CUSTOM` (`6 bytes`).

That distinction is important for review: this PR fixes the browser-to-server buffer transport boundary, but it does not change upstream ipywidgets serialization semantics for synced trait updates.

title: Fix issue #215: stabilize heavy ipyleaflet rerenders
description:

- before opening a widget comm, inspect that widget's serialized state
- recursively open any referenced child widget models first
- only then open the parent widget model

title: fix: avoid plotly rerender swap transient double roots
description:
## Summary

This PR fixes a Plotly `FigureWidget` rerender issue where the output briefly contains two direct `.lm-Widget` roots during a rerender swap.

That transient double-root state is enough to make Plotly measure against the wrong layout state, which matches the rerender jump/flicker described in issue `#208`.

## Changes

- serialize widget render work per output element so rerenders do not overlap on the same container
- mark previous widget roots as stale before mounting the new view
- keep stale roots out of layout while teardown finishes
- strengthen the Playwright regression so it samples the transient DOM state during rerenders instead of only checking for cleanup errors afterward

## Why this is narrow

This does not change widget comm ordering or teardown semantics.
It only changes how a rerendered output container swaps visible widget roots during `renderValue()`.

## Verification

- `../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -c tests/playwright/playwright-pytest.ini tests/playwright/plotly_rerender_cleanup/test_plotly_rerender_cleanup.py`
- `../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -c tests/playwright/playwright-pytest.ini tests/playwright/ipyleaflet_marker_click/test_ipyleaflet_marker_click.py tests/playwright/plotly_rerender_cleanup/test_plotly_rerender_cleanup.py`
- `git diff --check`

## Before / after behavior

Before this patch, the strengthened Plotly rerender regression fails because sampled rerenders observe `maxChildren == 2`.
After this patch, the same regression passes and the output stays at a single direct widget root throughout the swap.

title: fix: preserve child widget comm ordering for ipyleaflet updates
description:
## Summary
- delay `shinywidgets_comm_msg` until the reactive flush completes so child widget `comm_open` messages arrive before parent state updates that reference them
- add a Playwright regression based on the minimal `ipyleaflet` marker-click repro from #211
- add `ipyleaflet` to test dependencies for the new browser regression

## Why
The failing case is a parent widget update that introduces child widgets during the same flush. On current `main`, the browser can receive the parent `shinywidgets_comm_msg` before the child widget models exist client-side, which causes the first click marker update in `ipyleaflet` to be dropped and triggers the `state_change` error reported in #211.

This change keeps the client-side ordering consistent by sending mutation messages on `session.on_flushed(...)`, matching the point where newly created child widget comms have already been published.

## Additional context
During review, I checked this against Jupyter's comm model. In the reference Jupyter stack, `comm_open` creates the client-side comm/model first, and later `comm_msg` traffic assumes that comm already exists. JupyterLab's kernel connection also documents that kernel messages are handled in the order they are received, and that async handling pauses later message processing until the current handler completes. This change is therefore aligning Shiny's delivery timing with the ordering the Jupyter widget protocol already expects, rather than introducing a new assumption.

I also validated the issue outside the original `ipyleaflet` repro: on `main`, a parent widget update that introduces new child widget models can lag by one interaction in plain `ipywidgets` containers as well; with this change, those child models are available client-side before the parent mutation is applied.

Fixes #211

title: fix: harden widget teardown and add playwright regression coverage
description:
Closes #223

## Motivation

Re-rendering a widget output replaces the previous widget view with a new one. In practice, that teardown path could produce client-side cleanup noise during repeated rerenders, including errors like `Widget is not attached` and `no comm channel defined`.

The underlying problem is that some widget views need extra teardown before the model is closed, and some view cleanup code tries to sync state changes after the comm has already been torn down. That makes rerender behavior noisy even when the replacement itself succeeds.

## What This PR Changes

This PR hardens the client-side widget close path used during rerender:

- guards against models that do not have a `views` collection
- runs explicit view teardown for views that expose `destroy()`
- marks the model as no longer comm-live before `close()` so view cleanup does not try to sync `_view_count` over a dead comm
- suppresses only the two known teardown-noise patterns this PR is addressing, while continuing to log unexpected teardown failures
- triggers `comm:close` so the HTML manager releases its model reference

## Scope

This is a targeted rerender/teardown hardening change. It does not redesign the widget lifecycle or change how widgets are rendered when teardown is already clean.

It should also not be read as a full fix for the broader child-view failure discussed in `#215`. In local repros, this change removed the teardown-noise error but did not eliminate a separate `state_change` failure in an ipyleaflet-like reload scenario.

## Test Coverage

This PR adds Playwright regression coverage for repeated rerender across multiple widget types:

- plotly
- altair
- bokeh
- ipyleaflet

Each test verifies that repeated rerender leaves exactly one rendered widget in the output and does not emit the known teardown errors. The Playwright suite is also wired into GitHub Actions on Python 3.12.

## Reviewer Notes

The most important code is the `shinywidgets_comm_close` handler in `js/src/output.ts`. The key behavioral change is the ordering around teardown: perform any view-specific cleanup first, mark the comm inactive, then close the model and release the manager reference.

title: fix: Use render output's Context for widget cleanup instead of current Context
description:
## Summary

- Fixes widget cleanup registering on a temporary `reactive.isolate()` Context instead of the render output's Context, which caused premature `widget.close()` when upstream reactive sources invalidated
- `WidgetRenderContext` now captures the render Context at `__enter__` time and exposes it via `get_render_context()`
- `init_shiny_widget` uses the captured render Context for `on_close` registration instead of `get_current_context()`

## Root Cause

When a widget (e.g., `FigureWidget`) is constructed inside `reactive.isolate()`, `get_current_context()` returns the temporary isolate Context. When `reactive.poll` or any upstream reactive source fires, it invalidates this temporary Context, which triggers `on_close()` → `w.close()`, destroying the widget before the browser renders it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `examples/model-score` in py-shiny renders both Plotly charts correctly with streaming updates
- [ ] Verify that widgets created outside `reactive.isolate()` still clean up properly on re-render
- [ ] Verify that widgets created inside `reactive.isolate()` are only cleaned up when the render output re-executes, not when the isolate Context is invalidated

Closes #221

title: Allow for the `model_id` property to still be accessed after the widget is closed
description:
This problem was first discovered via https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinywidgets/issues/174

Here is a small reprex of the problem.

```python
from ipyleaflet import Map, Marker
from shiny import reactive
import shiny.express

from shinywidgets import render_widget

map = Map(zoom=2)

@render_widget
def map_out():
    reactive.invalidate_later(1)
    marker = Marker(location=(0, 0))
    map.add(marker)
    return map
```

After the 1st invalidation, you'll get:

```python
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'comm_id'
```

This happens because `.add()` reads of the `.model_id` property of every `Widget` instance (i.e., `Marker()`) that has ever been added to it. And, in recent versions of shinywidgets, we now `.close()` widgets when the reactive context they were initialized in get invalidated. When a widget gets closed, normally reading `.model_id` will result in error since that property reads `.comm.comm_id`, but `.comm` is `None`.

The workaround here is come up with a "mock" comm object that we add after close that allows for the `.model_id` property to still be read.

title: Ensure a session context is present when widgets are closed
description:
Closes #170

The reason this didn't come up in testing is because I was using an app that used `invalidate_later()` for invalidation, and it that case, the session is actually present `.on_invalidate()`. Whereas, if a reactive effect gets invalidated in the normal way, it apparently doesn't exist at `.on_invalidate()` time. 

This seems like a bug in Shiny, but since this is such a bad regression in shinywidgets, I'm gonna do this patch fix for now:

```python
from shiny import reactive
from shiny.express import input, ui
from shiny.reactive import get_current_context, invalidate_later
from shiny.session import get_current_session


@reactive.effect
def _():
    invalidate_later(1)

    # Prints the session, as expected
    ctx = get_current_context()
    ctx.on_invalidate(lambda: print(get_current_session()))


ui.input_action_button("btn", "Print session")


@reactive.effect
def _():
    input.btn()

    # Prints None?!?
    ctx = get_current_context()
    ctx.on_invalidate(lambda: print("Button click: ", get_current_session()))
```

title: Restore jQuery/$ directly instead of using noConflict() since the latter doesn't preserve event handlers
description:
A follow up to #38

Notice how, in this example, if you show the table, then change the slider the table renders again (while it's still hidden). Turns out this is because the `noConflict()` approach to restoring jQuery destroy's `shiny.js`'s event handers (to send output visibility when shown/hidden):

```py
from shiny import *
from ipyshiny import *
import ipywidgets as ipy

import seaborn as sns
import qgrid

iris = sns.load_dataset("iris")


app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.navset_tab(
        ui.nav("Slider", output_widget("s")), ui.nav("Widget", output_widget("widget"))
    ),
)


def server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):

    s = ipy.IntSlider(
        value=7,
        min=0,
        max=10,
        step=1,
        description="Test:",
        disabled=False,
        continuous_update=False,
        orientation="horizontal",
        readout=True,
        readout_format="d",
    )

    @output(name="s")
    @render_widget()
    def _():
        return s

    @output(name="widget")
    @render_widget()
    def _():
        print("Render widget: ", reactive_read(s, "value"))
        print("Is hidden: ", input[".clientdata_output_widget_hidden"]())
        return qgrid.show_grid(iris)

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

https://github.com/rstudio/ipyshiny/blob/ea98ce5c3206cb50af9417c5f19af846d6f90f5f/js/src/output.ts#L75-L81

title: fix: Track the rendering output per task, not per session
description:
Async `@render_widget` outputs can close each other's widgets once Shiny runs outputs concurrently (posit-dev/py-shiny#2549). This PR keeps "the output that is rendering now" per asyncio task instead of per session, so each render ties its widgets to its own output.

## Summary

[`WidgetRenderContext`](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinywidgets/pull/242/files#diff-7362b479e74e2db8536cf8ce5d68671cb936ad2b1c7612c83c6a82ef036b0f3c) now stores the rendering output and its reactive `Context` in a `ContextVar` instead of in `vars(session)`. Each asyncio task has its own copy of a `ContextVar`, so two renders that interleave at an `await` each see only their own value. `is_rendering_widget()` and `get_render_context()` no longer take a session argument. Their only caller is `init_shiny_widget()`.

Closes #241.

## Review notes

- **Only a problem after posit-dev/py-shiny#2549 merges.** Released py-shiny runs one output at a time, so the old per-session value was correct there. This change is safe to release before #2549.
- **A task started during a render** has a copy of the render's value. On exit, the render marks that value inactive, so a widget that such a task builds later is not tied to the output. This keeps the behavior of the old code, where the value was cleared on exit.
- **Modules also change.** With released py-shiny and released shinywidgets, a `@render_widget` in a Shiny module never closed its old widget on re-render. The render wrote the value to the module's session proxy, but `init_shiny_widget()` read it from the root session. Reading from the task fixes this too, and the changelog says so.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** `make check` passes (format, pyright, 89 unit tests). The [lifecycle tests](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinywidgets/pull/242/files#diff-2d11d962436925e7b3010828a1d92a9e5ee228a99416953bd7aea3648e9fede2) no longer inspect session variables. New tests cover interleaved renders, nested renders, and a task started during a render.
- **End to end:** I ran the #241 demo app in Chromium. With py-shiny from #2549, re-rendering Forecast no longer closes the Sales chart, and the server keeps 2 live widgets. With released py-shiny, the app behaves the same as before.
- **Mock sessions:** I drove sessions over a mock connection, against #2549 and against py-shiny main. Interleaved async renders and module re-renders now close the correct widget. 11 other checks give the same results as before the change: Plotly clicks, `reactive_read()`, background updates, two sessions, ipyleaflet, and message order.

title: fix: Show Shiny busy indicator over recalculating widget outputs
description:
Closes #213

## Summary

Shiny's busy indicator (spinner) is a CSS `:after` pseudo-element shown on outputs with the `.recalculating` class. shinywidgets sets inline `visibility: hidden` on the `.shiny-ipywidget-output` element — both when the widget value is `None`/null and while a plotly widget is settling — and since `visibility` inherits, the spinner was hidden too. This is why no spinner appeared in the issue's reprex: with `@reactive.event(input.submit)`, the output renders `None` until the first click, so `renderValue(null)` hides the element and every subsequent recalculation keeps the spinner hidden.

Shiny already solves this identical problem for htmlwidgets in `busy-indicators.css` (`.recalculating.html-widget-output { visibility: inherit !important; }`, etc.). This PR mirrors those rules for `.shiny-ipywidget-output` in `shinywidgets.css`:

- `.recalculating.shiny-ipywidget-output` gets `visibility: inherit !important`, so the element and spinner show during recalculation despite the inline style.
- Its children get `visibility: hidden`, hiding stale/empty widget content (same as htmlwidgets).
- Descendant `:after` pseudo-elements stay visible.

The rules are scoped to `[data-shiny-busy-spinners]`, so they're inert when busy indicators are disabled, and they only apply while recalculating — the anti-flicker hiding for `None` values and plotly settling is fully preserved at all other times.

## Verification

New Playwright test (`tests/playwright/busy_indicator/`) using the issue's reprex pattern: a slow `@reactive.event(input.submit)` calc feeding `@render_widget`. It asserts the initially-`None` widget is hidden, the spinner becomes visible during recalculation, and the widget renders and reveals afterward. The test fails without the CSS change and passes with it; the full Playwright suite (10 tests) and unit tests pass locally.

title: Add session_lifetime() and fix widget cleanup leaks
description:
## Why

Every re-render of a widget output currently leaks models. The `Layout`/`Style` models that ipywidgets creates lazily while serializing a widget are opened from a separate effect, so they get session lifetime instead of the render's: a re-rendering `VBox([Button, IntSlider, HTML])` goes from 14 live models to 84 after ten re-renders (server and browser alike), and keeps growing for the life of the session. Three smaller problems ride along: a widget closed before its deferred comm open is reopened anyway; comm messages are routed through whichever session is current (and the comm registry is shared process-wide, so a client can address another session's widgets); and there is no way to display the same widget again after its render was invalidated, which makes per-dataset widget caches impossible.

## What this gives you

- **Re-renders no longer leak.** Late-created defaults share the cleanup of the widget that created them. Counts stay flat across re-renders (14 → 14 in the fixture above).
- **`session_lifetime()`** (new, exported): construct widgets inside the block when you intend to display them again later.
  ```python
  @render_widget
  def plot():
      key = input.dataset()
      if key not in cache:
          with session_lifetime():
              cache[key] = make_plot(key)
      return cache[key]
  ```
  Returning a widget whose render has already been invalidated now raises an error that names `session_lifetime()`, instead of a 30-second timeout in the browser.

title: feat: session-owned widget lifetimes and session_lifetime()
description:
## What users get

**Reusable widgets.** Until now, every widget created while rendering an output was closed when that output re-rendered. There was no way to keep a widget alive, so caching one (say, one Plotly figure per dataset) was impossible: switching A → B → A rebuilt the widget from scratch and lost its state.

The new `session_lifetime()` context manager opts a widget out of that rule. Widgets constructed inside the block stay alive until the Shiny session ends:

```python
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from shinywidgets import render_plotly, session_lifetime

cache = {}

@render_plotly
def plot():
    name = input.dataset()
    if name not in cache:
        with session_lifetime():
            cache[name] = go.FigureWidget(make_figure(name))
    return cache[name]
```

Three things to know:

- Only **newly constructed** widgets get the session's lifetime. Putting an existing widget inside the block does not adopt it.
- A widget belongs to the session that created it, so keep one cache per session: widgets can't be shared across sessions.
- Rendering a widget whose render has ended (or that you closed yourself) now raises a clear error that points at `session_lifetime()`, instead of showing stale or broken output. **This is the breaking change**: if you reuse a widget across re-renders today, move its construction inside `session_lifetime()`.

**Two reliability fixes** come along for free:

- A widget closed before its initialization finished (for example, a fast re-render or a session ending right after construction) no longer reopens itself in the browser.
- Widget messages can no longer go through the wrong browser session. Each session now owns its widgets and talks only to its own client.

This is phase 1 of the widget lifecycle overhaul (design: lifetimes as roots; dependency collection and browser epochs follow in stacked PRs).

## What changed (technical)

- **`session_lifetime()`** (new public API): widgets constructed inside the block belong to the current Shiny session instead of the ambient render. Exiting the block restores the previous construction policy and does not close anything; referencing an existing widget inside the block does not adopt it. Raises clearly without an active session; is a no-op on the Express stub pass.
- **Per-session `SessionLifecycle`** (`shinywidgets/_lifecycle.py`) owns widget records, lifetimes, and an instance-owned `ShinyCommManager` per root session. Managers live in a `WeakKeyDictionary` and are explicitly removed at session end.
- **Durable render lifetimes**: each render captures a `Lifetime` before any widget construction (retired when the render's `Context` invalidates). Construction selection precedence: explicit selection → current render → root session. Child tasks retain the inherited construction lifetime after the render block exits; retired selections raise instead of silently becoming session-owned.
- **Reliable cancellation**: `PendingShinyComm` makes pre-initialization close observable, so closing a widget (explicitly or via render retirement) cancels its scheduled comm-open instead of being resurrected.
- **Session-captured comms**: `ShinyComm` publishes through its originating session's flush hooks, not the ambient session; comms unregister by ID *and* identity; session termination disables sends before closing records.
- **Display validation**: rendering a widget whose render lifetime has ended raises `This widget's render lifetime has ended. Create reusable widgets inside session_lifetime().`; cross-session widgets are rejected, including cached widgets whose owning lifecycle has been collected. Reusing a model ID cannot make a closed widget displayable: the live record must own the exact widget instance. Closed-widget metadata is kept as inert tombstones in an identity-keyed weak map (supports unhashable widgets like plotly's `FigureWidget`), and the initializer closure no longer retains closed widgets for the session's lifetime.
- **Close overrides run once**: comm-close notifications cannot re-enter a widget's non-idempotent cleanup override, and later repeated closes reuse the completed close. A generic regression exercises widget-, comm-, and session-initiated closure without Bokeh.
- **No deprecated ipywidgets API**: registry cleanup reads the module-level `_instances` dict (8.0.3+) / `Widget._active_widgets` (8.0.0–8.0.2) directly instead of `Widget.widgets`, which is deprecated and warns on every access.

## Preserved behavior

Phases 1–2 intentionally keep the existing browser clearing counter and #246's view WeakMap. No JS/runtime/dependency changes.

## Evidence

- Red/green: `test_explicit_close_cancels_pending_open` failed on main (comm registry still held the closed widget) and passes now.
- 119 unit tests pass (`make check`), including 25 real-session lifecycle tests (nesting, exception/cancellation restoration, interleaved async renders, non-adoption, module root-session ownership, stub pass, GC non-retention, cross-session rejection).
- Explicit `pyright` on the new typed tests: 0 errors.
- Full Playwright suite in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit passes (26 + 52), including the retained popup, GeoJSON-hover, dynamic-UI, module rerender, busy-indicator, Plotly afterplot, and all six #246 view-retention cases.

Stack: #248 → #252 → #254 → #255 → #256 → #253.

GitHub CI passes on Python 3.10–3.14, including the full Chromium suite on 3.12.

## Review follow-up

The three ownership findings were reproduced against the dependency collector, browser lease protocol, and downstream integration branches before applying the fixes. Five regression cases cover expired ownership, model-ID reuse after retirement, child construction before and after retirement, and explicit session lifetime selection. The fixes and changelog entries are propagated through #252, #254, #255, #256, #253, #249, and draft #257. Full Python checks pass on the lifecycle and Bokeh/Panel branches; all 55 Chromium cases pass on the integrated #254 stack.

The newly published #257 validation branch also retains these ownership fixes. Its Python checks pass (141 tests), and a focused ipywidgets 8.0.0 runtime check passes for pending close, open close, render retirement, registry cleanup, and comm trait restoration. It remains draft with its separately documented Plotly cache-update, Bokeh/WebKit, and minimum-version validation blockers. Its Chromium CI also fails on the retained Leaflet popup test with `Cannot convert undefined or null to object`; the original fc5d869 CI run failed on the identical test and error before these review fixes.

title: fix: collect widget models from live roots and dependencies
description:
## Problem

Phase 1 (#248) retired a render by closing every widget constructed during it. That's wrong when a live shared widget references one of those widgets — e.g., an `ipyleaflet` popup retained for the session whose `Layout`/`Style` is first materialized while a *temporary* map is being serialized. Closing by construction membership kills the shared popup's style. Conversely, unreachable widget-reference cycles and headless `jslink()` models must not survive retirement.

This is phase 2 of the widget lifecycle overhaul (stacked on #248). Browser lease/epoch work is phase 3; this phase preserves the existing browser cleanup and transport ordering.

## What changed

- **Root/edge collection**: retiring a render now releases its roots and collects records unreachable from the remaining live roots (session roots + other active render roots). Edges come from *materialized* synced trait values via `shinywidgets/_widget_dependencies.py` — actual `Widget` objects in dict/list/tuple containers, never literal `IPY_MODEL_...` strings, never by invoking lazy default factories, serializers, `get_state()`, or `_repr_mimebundle_()`. Mark/sweep handles cycles; edges are refreshed before every collection, so in-place container mutations are accounted for.
- **Deferred preparation runs under the record's own lifetime** (`use_lifetime(record.lifetime)`), so late-created defaults share the record's fate and are collectible — fixing the "five default models escape render cleanup" leak — while surviving when reachable from live roots (the borrowed popup style). Preparation failure closes the record instead of leaving it pending.
- **The inherited `_repr_mimebundle_()` hook is no longer called during preparation.** The base implementation only builds a discarded MIME bundle and `repr()`s the widget, which recurses infinitely on widget-reference cycles (this crashed the effect and took the whole session down via Shiny's unhandled-error path). Genuine overrides (plotly's state normalization, verified against installed plotly 6.7.0) still run.
- **Opaque dependency policy (review decision)**: a live widget whose custom trait serializer hides dependencies without a registered adapter makes the graph incomplete. Per the plan's recommended fallback, collection then **retains records and emits one `RuntimeWarning`** rather than risk premature closes; a later complete snapshot resumes collection; session close remains unconditional. (The alternative was strict failure via `UnsupportedWidgetGraphError`; the plan recommends retention. Flagging here for review.)
- **Adapter + disposer contracts**: `DependencyAdapter` (keyed by serializer identity) supplies hidden dependencies; lazily registered scalar adapters for verified serializers (ipywidgets `date_to_json`, plotly `_py_to_js`, jupyter_bokeh `render_bundle` — implementations inspected; none can contain widget references). `add_disposer()` registers non-model resource cleanup (e.g., a Python `link()`'s `unlink`) owned by a lifetime, run once after admission closes.

## Evidence

- Red→green: `test_session_root_protects_temporary_dependency` and `test_borrowed_late_default_survives_render_retirement` fail under phase-1 membership closing, pass with collection. The cycle test initially crashed the session via the repr recursion, motivating the `_repr_mimebundle_` selection change.
- 131 unit tests pass (`make check`); explicit pyright on the new typed tests: 0 errors.
- Browser suite (chromium/firefox/webkit) for `ipyleaflet_rerender_cleanup`, `ipyleaflet_popup_html_child`, `ipyleaflet_geojson_hover`, `dynamic_ui_widget`, `widget_view_retention`: 30 passed — #237's nested-child/popup fixes and #246's view retention are preserved with the new dependency decisions.

## Out of scope (phase 3/4)

Acknowledged view replacement/leases, browser epochs, and the package support matrix. The opaque-serializer retention diagnostic may fire for third-party widgets with unadapted custom serializers; the phase 4 matrix will document them.

title: feat: epoch-bound managers, presentation mounts, and display leases
description:
## Problem

On main, browser cleanup is connection-wide and blunt: `clear_state()` snapshots pending model promises and replaces the whole registry, so a pending clear can **remove a model registered after the clear began**, and cancels a **fresh parent's** late-child lookup (it becomes an `ErrorWidget`). Views are tracked in a per-element WeakMap with no server acknowledgement, so the server closes models before the browser has actually replaced the presentation. Both failure modes are reproduced as tests in this PR (and then fixed).

This is phase 3 of the widget lifecycle overhaul (stacked on #252). It replaces the browser implementation coherently: runtime construction, dependency loading, epoch-bound managers, presentation mounts, the display-lease protocol, test fixtures, asset-refresh tooling, and distributed assets.

## What changed

**Source-built runtime** (`js/src/runtime.ts`): one coherent compilation of the official `@jupyter-widgets` packages plus the internals the lifecycle code uses (`ManagerBase`/`serialize_state`, Lumino, JupyterLab rendermime/outputarea, base `OutputView`, HTML `OutputModel`), replacing the downloaded libembed-amd.js. `runtime-register.js` defines the official AMD module IDs as static aliases so third-party widgets share the exact same constructors (verified in-browser: shared constructor identity, single Backbone per widget generation matching the official bundle's base7/base6 split, zero font/module 404s). `scripts/static_download.R` now regenerates from source instead of overwriting the runtime with a downloaded bundle. jupyterlab deps deduplicated to single versions.

**Epoch-bound managers** (`js/src/lifecycle/manager.ts`): one `EpochManager extends ManagerBase` per transport epoch with an owned canonical registry (never upstream `_models`). Retirement is permanent and synchronous: lookup/registration/construction reject with `EpochRetiredError` (never a successful ErrorWidget fallback), identity-checked close listeners can't remove a fresh same-ID record, waiters reject promptly, and fresh-epoch work never awaits old pending loaders. Frontend `new_widget()` without a comm is an explicit failure (measured: the old dummy comm never reached `new_model`).

**Presentation mounts** (`mount.ts`, `mime.ts`, `output.ts`): output mounts own root/child views, observers, timers, and tasks. `renderValue` synchronously records a candidate task (never awaits protocol/model round-trips inside Shiny's dispatch queue); once the candidate has a claimed lease and a prepared view, the old presentation is removed through its mount and the new one attaches. Nested Output widget MIME renderings get explicit child mount scopes via an owned `OutputArea`/`RenderMimeRegistry`. The plotly reveal, fill handling, popup resize, busy-indicator, and dynamic-binding behaviors are preserved (full suite green in 3 engines).

**Display leases** (Python + browser): publications/offers/leases per output on the session lifecycle; a versioned, idempotent claim/release protocol. Claims bind provisional or renewed leases atomically (superseded/cancelled/stale refused; replays return recorded outcomes; collected roots are never resurrected — a cached replay of a collected widget renders the `session_lifetime()` guidance error). Replacement/null/error/unbind release the exact lease only after presentation removal; released leases make unreachable models collectible. Claim sequences are per output/epoch so DOM rebind renews correctly.

## Preserved fixes

Every #237 waiter case has an explicit epoch-based successor; all six #246 view cases keep their disposal/cached-model-identity assertions through mount instrumentation; popup, GeoJSON-hover, dynamic-UI, busy-indicator, and Plotly afterplot tests all pass with the new runtime. No production diagnostic global — tests route-instrument the served bundle's `createWidgetLifecycle()` line.

## Compatibility notes

- The wire protocol is versioned (`sw: 1` envelopes; qualified model IDs `sw-<namespace>-<id>`). Package and bundle ship together; legacy/foreign packets are rejected (foreign well-formed packets are dropped with a warning, malformed ones are hard errors).
- A widget displayed from a cache must now be created inside `session_lifetime()`; otherwise its redisplay after collection fails with the documented error. This is the intended breaking contract.
- `ipywidgets.Output.clear_output()` and `with out: display(...)` route through the IPython kernel and were already no-ops outside it; fixtures use the supported `append_display_data` / `out.outputs` assignment.
- **Reconnect**: fresh-session reload works cleanly (fresh namespace/epoch). Shiny's in-page `reconnect()` currently fails **upstream** on cached output-progress state ("unexpected state of: 'value'") — captured as evidence, not worked around; a narrowly scoped py-shiny investigation is warranted. Hosted same-session resume has **no public hook** (py-shiny creates a new session per WebSocket); documented as an explicit unsupported-resume policy blocker.

## Evidence

- Red→green: reproduction tests showed the pending-clear model removal and fresh-parent ErrorWidget on the old manager; their epoch successors assert the opposite and pass.
- 135 unit tests (`make check`), explicit pyright on typed lifecycle tests: 0 errors.
- Full Playwright suite: **165 passed across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit** (including new lifecycle_epochs/mounts/leases/output_mime/reconnect/anywidget suites and all preserved fixtures).
- `uv build` wheel inspected (all runtime/register/font assets packaged) and a served app exercised from the installed wheel.

Requirements-to-test mapping is in the phase plan notes; per-test details in the new fixture docstrings.

title: Add render_matplotlib() for matplotlib via ipympl
description:
## Summary

Matplotlib is the plotting library most Python users reach for first. Until now, the only way to show a figure in Shiny was the static image from `@render.plot`. This PR adds `@render_matplotlib`, which renders figures as interactive [ipympl](https://matplotlib.org/ipympl/) widgets with pan, zoom and the toolbar, and supports `reactive_read()` like any other widget.

- `as_widget()` now coerces a matplotlib `Figure` (or an `Axes`, via its figure) into an ipympl `Canvas`. That covers anything that produces a matplotlib figure: seaborn, `pandas.DataFrame.plot()`, scikit-learn displays, statsmodels plots, and so on. It also handles 3D and custom `Axes` subclasses and axes that live in a `SubFigure`. seaborn's figure-level functions (`relplot()`, `jointplot()`, …) work too, via the figure their grid holds. Requires `pip install ipympl`.
- In filling layouts, figures resize to fit their container.
- Figures created through pyplot are deregistered (`plt.close()`) when their widget retires, so repeated re-renders don't leak figures or trigger "More than 20 figures" warnings.
- Returning a figure whose canvas is already a live ipympl `Canvas`, or returning that `Canvas` itself, reuses it, along with its toolbar and header settings and its lifetime. A returned `Canvas` also gets a `FigureManager` and pyplot cleanup, like a coerced figure.

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from shiny import App, ui
from shinywidgets import output_widget, render_matplotlib

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(output_widget("plot"))

def server(input, output, session):
    @render_matplotlib
    def plot():
        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
        ax.plot([1, 2, 3])
        return fig

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

`examples/matplotlib/app.py` is a fuller tour, shown next to `@render.plot` for contrast: zoom and pan, selecting points through a matplotlib callback that drives a table, and updating a figure in place without losing the current zoom.

## ipympl quirks this works around

ipympl was built for Jupyter, and a few of its assumptions don't hold in Shiny. Each workaround below is small and has a regression test.

- **pyplot's backend stays put.** On import, ipympl selects itself as pyplot's backend ([matplotlib/ipympl#623](https://github.com/matplotlib/ipympl/issues/623)). Left alone, the first `render_matplotlib()` would turn every later pyplot figure in the process into a widget, including those drawn for Shiny's own `@render.plot`. `matplotlib.use()` is now a no-op while ipympl's backend is imported.
- **The first paint is immediate.** ipympl sends its initial image from its display hook, which #277 stopped calling for non-plotly widgets. Without that hook, canvases started blank and logged `drawImage` errors. The hook is now called for ipympl again.
- **Old figures are fully removed.** ipympl's canvas view overrides `remove()` without calling the base implementation. Re-renders leaked the old view and left its fill `ResizeObserver` resizing a retired figure, and a container whose children changed left the old figure on screen. The view class is now patched so `remove()` also runs the base implementation.
- **Figures are the right size on any display.** On macOS, pyplot's native backend doubles a figure's dpi on Retina screens. That doubling used to carry over into the widget, so in a 1x browser fonts and lines came out twice their size. Coercion now resets it, and ipympl applies the browser's own pixel ratio.
- **A `FigureManager` is always attached.** The canvas gets one, as `%matplotlib widget` does. Without it, ipympl's browser messages (e.g. resize) crash.

Known, not addressed: a canvas reused across renders gains one set of ipympl model listeners per view, and when an ipywidgets container drops a canvas, the canvas's toolbar view isn't removed (it's invisible). Neither can be cleaned up without reaching into ipympl internals.

## Also included: fill/resize registry refactor (#272)

ipympl is the third widget with its own fill/resize special case, so this PR also consolidates them, with no behavior change. Per-package browser behavior (plotly's settle-then-reveal, ipympl's auto-resize, quak's fill classes) moves into a registry in `js/src/fill.ts`. The plotly/altair branches of `set_layout_defaults()` become a table keyed by package. Reviewed in #272.

## Verification

- Unit tests (182 passed, 1 pre-existing xfail): coercion paths, canvas reuse and lifetime, the comm-open state carrying the initial image, a fresh-process check that coercion leaves pyplot's backend and open figures alone, and dpi handling across pixel ratios.
- Playwright: the canvas draws pixels, re-renders don't accumulate canvases, the figure fills and tracks its container, re-renders release old views and ResizeObservers, and a canvas dropped from a container leaves the screen. The full suite (68 tests) passes with current `main` merged in.

title: Add render_maplibre() for maplibre via anywidget
description:

```python
from maplibre import Map
from shiny import App, ui
from shinywidgets import output_widget, render_maplibre

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(output_widget("map"))

def server(input, output, session):

```

title: Rename render_hvplot() -> render_holoviews(); expand HoloViews browser-test coverage
description:
## Summary

This PR started as a bokeh-based route to HoloViews support (`render_holoviews()` via `holoviews.render(x, backend="bokeh")`), but #253 landed first with a panel-based route (`render_hvplot`). After comparing both approaches in a real browser, this PR now consolidates on the panel-based implementation and becomes:

- **Renames `render_hvplot()` → `render_holoviews()`** for discoverability (users holding a holoviews object shouldn't have to know to search for "hvplot"). Safe to rename since #253 is still unreleased. Applies to the renderer, tests, Playwright apps, and changelog.
- **Expanded Playwright coverage** (`tests/playwright/render_holoviews`): a range of real examples — holoviews `Curve`, `Overlay`, side-by-side `Layout`, `.opts()` (verified via actual canvas pixel colors), `DynamicMap`, and hvPlot (line + grouped scatter with legend) — asserting canvases actually draw pixels in a real browser, plus re-render lifecycle (no view leaks) and no console errors.
- **A Playwright test proving `DynamicMap` interactivity works**: changing the kdim slider/spinner round-trips to the Python server (via shinywidgets' comm layer servicing panel's bokeh document callbacks) and re-renders the plot.

## Why panel-based over this PR's original bokeh-based approach

Both paths use `jupyter_bokeh.BokehModel` as the widget transport, so they only differ in how the holoviews object becomes a bokeh model: `hv.render()` vs panel's HoloViews pane. That difference turns out to be decisive:

- **`hv.render()` silently degrades `DynamicMap`/`HoloMap`** to a static first frame — no widget, no way to explore the dimension. Panel's pane instead renders the plot *with* kdim widgets, and those widgets genuinely work in shinywidgets (verified in Chromium): the Python callback round-trips and the plot updates. So HoloViews server-side interactivity is largely preserved by the panel path and entirely dropped by the bokeh path.
- **Dependency story is a wash**: `hvplot` already hard-depends on `panel>=1.0`, so the bokeh path's "no panel needed" advantage only helps pure-holoviews users (and the fix is just `pip install panel`).
- **One canonical path** avoids a permanent "which renderer do I use?" docs/support burden, and panel is the ecosystem-supported route (it's what HoloViz itself tests against).
- The bokeh path's one surviving advantage — no panel↔bokeh version coupling (panel pins bokeh) — applies to hvplot users regardless, since panel is installed either way.

## Verification

- `ruff` format ✅, pyright ✅, 150 unit tests ✅
- 17 Playwright tests (Chromium) across `render_holoviews`, `bokeh_express`, `bokeh_extensions`, `bokeh_dependencies`, `render_maplibre` ✅
- Visual confirmation of all 7 example outputs rendering with toolbars, and of the `DynamicMap` slider re-rendering the plot at a new kdim value

```python
import holoviews as hv
from shiny import App, ui
from shinywidgets import output_widget, render_holoviews

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(output_widget("plot"))

def server(input, output, session):
    @render_holoviews
    def plot():
        # DynamicMaps render with working kdim widgets
        return hv.DynamicMap(lambda n: hv.Curve([0, n, 2 * n]), kdims="n").redim.range(n=(1, 5))

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

title: Dispose widget views when outputs are replaced or cleared
description:
Repeatedly rendering a widget output now releases its previous displayed view instead of leaving detached views in the browser manager's resize list. This also handles returning the same widget instance across renders, clearing an output with `None`, and recovering from a render error while keeping reusable models alive.

The previous DOM-removal path could leave Lumino believing that a disconnected widget was still attached, interrupting disposal before the manager received its removal event. The binding now removes the old view through its public lifecycle before replacing the output content. The served JavaScript bundle is rebuilt.

Existing ipyleaflet popup-child teardown errors and lazy default-model retention remain under separate investigation, related to #215. This PR addresses the detached displayed views; it does not close #215 or change widget model ownership.

title: Suppress a widget's close once a newer comm owns its id (reused explicit model_id)
description:
## Summary

Addresses the remaining Copilot review feedback from #260.

A widget constructed with an explicit `model_id` keeps that id when it is re-created on re-render. The old widget's `comm_close` is sent `on_flushed` — *after* the replacement's `comm_open`, by design (avoids flicker) — so the browser looked the model up by id and tore down the **new** model, leaving the output blank. This failure mode predates #260 (same behavior on `main`); #260's `closedModels.delete()` on `comm_open` handles the marker side, and this PR handles the stale-close side.

## Changes

- `ShinyComm.close()` schedules its close with a send-time guard: if a *different* comm has re-registered the id by the time the `on_flushed` send runs, the close is suppressed. A legitimately closed comm still sends (it unregisters itself before send time, and an unregistered id does not suppress).
- `ShinyCommManager.unregister_comm()` no longer pops a registry entry that belongs to a newer comm.
- Unit test for the suppression + a Playwright test (`tests/playwright/reopened_model_id/`) that re-renders an explicit-`model_id` widget and asserts it stays rendered. Verified the Playwright test fails without the `_comm.py` change.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/unit` (115 passed, 1 xfailed — pre-existing xfail)
- [x] New Playwright test passes with fix, fails without it

title: Raise a clear error when a render returns another session's (or a closed) widget
description:
Caching a widget at module scope so every visitor shares it is an easy mistake to make. Until now it failed silently: the first session worked, and every other session's output sat "recalculating" for 30 seconds, then went blank. The same happened when a fresh container held a child from another session, or a child that had already been closed. Now the render fails right away, and the output shows:

> IntSlider belongs to another Shiny session (or was closed), so it can't be displayed here. Construct widgets per session.

The session that owns the widget keeps working.

### How

Before `_render()` returns a widget, it walks the widget's tree and raises if any widget is closed or isn't registered to the current (root-scoped) session. The walk follows the same rule as the cleanup sweep, so the traversal is now a single shared `walk_widget_tree()`, and `referenced_widgets()` is built on top of it. The check is skipped when there's no real session (Express's stub pass, or tests that call `_render()` directly). A widget built with `session_lifetime()` is still displayable in its own session.

`_render_widget_base` imports `foreign_or_closed_widget` inside the function, because `_shinywidgets` already imports from `_render_widget_base` at module scope.

### Testing

- Unit tests: a foreign root, a foreign child, and a closed child all raise. They fail on #261 with `DID NOT RAISE`. Same-session `session_lifetime()` widgets and stub sessions are unaffected.
- `cross_session` (Playwright): session A caches an `IntSlider` at module scope, shown both directly and inside a `VBox`. Session B gets the error in both outputs within 5 s, and session A still updates afterwards. On #261, session B's outputs stay blank.

`make check` passes (114 passed, 1 xfailed). The full Chromium Playwright suite has 31 passed.

title: Close remaining widget cleanup gaps: kept children, background tasks, session end, sweep cost
description:
#258's cleanup has a few gaps. This PR closes them:

- **A container's dropped children now get cleaned up.** A session-owned container that rebuilds its child on every render used to leak: the old child is still referenced when its render ends, so it was kept, and it was never checked again. It now gets re-checked at the next sweep. Measured in a real browser: the server model count stays flat across re-renders, where #258 grew to 26 models (vs 8 here). This is the one pattern where #258 leaked more than `main`.
- **Widgets built by a render's background tasks close with that render.** For example, an `asyncio` task streaming markers into a map. They used to live until the session ended.
- **Closing a session no longer breaks other code that still references its widgets.** Widgets closed at session end now keep a usable `model_id`, as render cleanup already did, so a later read no longer raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'comm_id'`.
- **The cleanup sweep stays fast at scale.** It now walks only the session's own widgets, and only traits that can hold widget references. Measured on the edge-case apps: 220 → 10 ms with 20 sessions × 1,000 markers, and 76 → 0.3 ms for a large GeoJSON layer.
- **Fixed a latent ordering bug:** a widget built in a render that was already invalidated now gets closed instead of landing on an orphaned list.

### Testing

- `borrowed_dropped` (Playwright): fails on #258 (`assert 26 == 8`) and passes here.
- `session_churn` (Playwright): opens and closes 10 real browser sessions, then checks that an 11th session's state matches a fresh first session's (comm managers, session widget map, render-owned and kept widgets). It uses real sessions because Shiny invalidates a session's outputs *after* `on_ended` cleanup runs, and that ordering is what per-session global state has to survive. #258 already passes this scenario; the test is here to catch regressions.
- New unit tests for each fix, each written to fail first. One existing test encoded the background-task behavior that this PR changes; it was inverted.
- `test_widget_close_guard.py` checks the three ways a widget can be closed (`widget.close()`, `widget.comm.close()`, session end). For each, shinywidgets never calls `close()` an extra time, nothing raises, and the widget leaves the registry. Widget- and session-initiated closure pass. **Comm-initiated closure is marked `xfail`:** ipywidgets' `Widget` never registers `comm.on_close()`, so closing only the comm never runs the widget's `close()`. That's the same on `main` and isn't fixed here.

`make check` passes (109 passed, 1 xfailed). The full Chromium Playwright suite has 30 passed.

### Notes

- `close_render_widgets()` now skips widgets with `is_closed_widget()` instead of `comm is None`. Session-end cleanup now leaves an `OrphanedShinyComm` behind, and Shiny invalidates the session's outputs afterwards, so the old check would have closed those widgets a second time. There's a test for this.
- The `_RenderingWidget` wrapper is removed. It only existed to carry the `active` flag, and dropping that flag is what ties background-task widgets to their render.
- In one existing test (`test_reference_walk_tolerates_container_cycles`), the trait that holds the widget reference now has the `widget_serialization` tag. That's the only kind of trait the sweep now follows, and the test still covers cycles.

title: Fix widget view-lifecycle bugs: render.ui show/hide hang, dynamic UI view leak, ipyleaflet re-render errors
description:
## Mental model

Every on-screen widget involves two separate things:

- **Model** — the widget's *state*: a JS mirror of the Python object, synced over comm messages. Its lifetime is owned by the server (`comm_open` / `comm_close`).
- **View** — the *DOM representation* of a model. One model can have many views, and views form trees: a container's view creates child views (`VBox` → `Label`), and ipyleaflet's map view creates marker/layer views plus a native Leaflet object with its own timers and listeners. ipywidgets doesn't track child views anywhere — and before this PR, nothing owned view lifetime at all.

The three bugs fixed here share one root cause: teardown signals reached the *model* and the *DOM* but not the *views*:

| Event | Model heard it | DOM heard it | Views heard it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Widget re-renders / output removed | ✓ `comm_close` | ✓ element replaced | ✗ |
| `render.ui` hides a panel | ✓ closed while hidden | ✓ unbound | ✗ |

The fix makes view lifetime *derived*: a view is alive iff its element is bound, its model is open, and its ancestors are alive. All teardown triggers (`comm_close`, `renderValue` replacing content, `shiny:unbound`) now route through one removal path, and the manager tracks every view it creates (`_liveViews`) so removal sweeps the whole subtree (`removeViewTree`) instead of just the root. Two "gravestone" sets cover the async edges: a child view that finishes creating after its parent was removed tears itself down (`_removedViews`), and `renderValue` on a replayed value that names a closed model renders nothing instead of waiting (`closedModels`).

The manager-side tracking and teardown triggers live in `js/src/output.ts`; the view-teardown helpers that reach into third-party internals (Lumino's message protocol, ipyleaflet's Leaflet map, plotly <6's `FigureView`) live in `js/src/views.ts`. No Python changes. This lands first in the widget-cleanup series; #258 and its follow-ups are the Python side.

## Bugs fixed

- **Re-showing a hidden widget hung the page.** Hide a `@render.ui` panel, change an input the hidden widget depends on, then show the panel again: the widget never came back, and the page waited 30 s on a model the server had already closed. It now re-renders right away. The same fix covers `remove_ui()` followed by `insert_ui()` of the same output.
- **Dynamic UI leaked widget views.** When dynamic UI removed a widget output, its view stayed alive and kept receiving model updates, so a session-owned widget toggled 5 times ended up with 6 live views. Now it keeps 1.
- **Re-rendering an ipyleaflet map threw errors and leaked listeners.** Every re-render threw uncaught page errors ("Widget is not attached" / "Cannot convert undefined or null to object" from late `moveend` handlers) and leaked the old map's native Leaflet instance and its child views: about 100 listeners per re-render. Now there are no errors and the listener count stays flat.

## Testing

Three new Playwright tests. Each one fails against `main`'s bundle and passes with this change:

| test | on `main`'s bundle | with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render_ui_toggle` | widget never reappears (5 s locator timeout; actual hang is 30 s) | reappears |
| `session_widget_toggle` | `expected exactly 1 live view, got [6]` | 1 view |
| `container_child_views` | 7× `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` | no errors |

`make check` passes. The full Chromium Playwright suite has 29 passed. The bundle is rebuilt with `yarn build` and adds no new bundled modules.

## Notes for reviewers

- The plotly `destroy()` + `delete model` hack from #169 moved from the `comm_close` handler into `disposeNative`, so it now fires on every teardown path. It previously only ran when `comm_close` arrived before view removal unregistered the view from `model.views`. This is a no-op for plotly >=6 (its `FigureWidget` is anywidget-based, and `AnyView.remove()` cleans up properly); the duck-typed `hasDestroy()` check preserves it for plotly 5.x, which is still within the declared `plotly>=5.0.0` floor.
- View-tree removal applies to every container view (VBox, Tab, …), not only ipyleaflet. The existing `widget_view_retention` tests, which cover cached and shared widgets, still pass.
- `closedModels` grows by one string per closed model for the life of the page. Left unbounded on purpose; cheap to bound if that matters.
- In the `session_widget_toggle` test app, a hidden static `output_widget` makes `output.js` load with the page. Without it, the test hits a separate existing bug: a widget shown only via `render.ui` can stay blank. Out of scope here.

title: Formally deprecate register_widget()
description:
## Summary

Closes #127.

`register_widget()` doesn't follow the Shiny rendering pattern (calling a register method inside the server body doesn't read as "this will be rendered to the UI"), and its docstring has said "Deprecated. Use @render_widget instead." for a while — but no actual warning was emitted, so users had no signal at runtime.

Now it emits a deprecation warning (`ShinyDeprecationWarning` from shiny, falling back to `DeprecationWarning` on older shiny versions) pointing users at the `@render_widget` pattern:

```python
# Deprecated
map_widget = register_widget("map", map)

# Recommended
@render_widget
def map():
    return map_val
```

- `shinywidgets/_shinywidgets.py`: `register_widget()` now warns on every call.
- `tests/unit/test_widget_bootstrap.py`: existing `register_widget` tests assert the warning; added a dedicated deprecation test.

title: Warn when a plotly figure with frames is rendered (frames are dropped)
description:

title: feat: accept (figure, config) tuple in @render_plotly
description:

## Summary

There was no way to pass Plotly.js [config options](https://plotly.com/javascript/configuration-options/) (e.g., hiding the modebar) through `@render_plotly`. Following the suggestion in the issue thread, the render function may now return a Dash-style `(figure, config)` tuple — the same shape as `dcc.Graph(figure=..., config=...)`, so it's familiar and LLM-friendly:

```python
@render_plotly
def plot():
    fig = px.histogram(px.data.tips(), x="total_bill")
    return fig, {"displayModeBar": False}
```

Implementation:

- `render_widget_base` now routes coercion through an overridable `_as_widget()` hook (behavior unchanged for all other renderers).
- `render_plotly._as_widget()` detects a 2-tuple with a dict second element, coerces the figure as usual, then merges `config` into the `FigureWidget`'s synced `_config` trait. The merge order means user config takes precedence over shinywidgets' own defaults (e.g., `{"responsive": False}` is honored), while plotly's own defaults (e.g., `plotlyServerURL`) are preserved. Non-tuple returns flow through unchanged, so this is fully backwards compatible.

## Verification

- New unit tests in `tests/unit/test_render_widget.py`: tuple config is honored, user config overrides the `responsive` default, plain figure return is unaffected. Full suite: 153 passed.
- New Playwright test (`tests/playwright/plotly_config/`): `displayModeBar: False` hides the modebar in the browser while a default plot keeps it; existing plotly Playwright tests (`plotly_cached_figurewidget`, `plotly_rerender_cleanup`) still pass.
- `make pyright` clean, ruff format/lint clean.

title: Unify per-package fill/resize behavior into registries
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to #249 (stacked on `mpl-widget`; retarget to `main` once that merges). No behavior change — this is a pure refactor that consolidates the per-package fill/resize special-casing that #249 added a third instance of.

- New `js/src/fill.ts`: a `WIDGET_BEHAVIORS` registry keyed by `widget_pkg` with three hooks: `hideUntilSettled` (keep output hidden until `onDisplayed` reveals it), `setupFill` (fill-container setup; may return a cleanup that the binding wires to view removal), and `onDisplayed` (post-display behavior; defaults to the window-resize dispatch). Migrates the three existing inline special cases: plotly's settle-then-reveal, ipympl's auto-resize, and quak's shadow-DOM fill classes. The binding now owns the shared machinery (`_onImplementation` waiting, the view-staleness guard, cleanup wiring) once instead of per call site.
- `shinywidgets/_render_widget_base.py`: the plotly/altair branches of `set_layout_defaults()` become a `_LAYOUT_DEFAULTS` registry keyed by `widget_pkg()`, mirroring the existing `AS_WIDGET_MAP` pattern. bokeh intentionally stays in `as_widget_bokeh()` (its `sizing_mode` hack doesn't work from `set_layout_defaults()`, per the existing TODO).

## Key decisions

- Widgets are now identified by `data.widget_pkg` (computed server-side) everywhere, replacing the one-off `model.get("_model_module")` check added in #249. One consequence: an ipympl `Canvas` subclass defined in a package other than `ipympl` would no longer get auto-resize. Judged acceptable (no known cases); the alternative is keying the registry on `_model_module` instead.
- The plotly reveal path moves verbatim into the registry; its render-token staleness checks are expressed via the `isStale()`/`reveal()` callbacks provided to `onDisplayed`.
- Deliberately not abstracted: `setupMplAutoResize` itself (one consumer; generalize when a second widget needs container-driven resize).

## Verification

- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `make pyright` (0 errors), `tsc --noEmit`, and the rebuilt bundle matches the committed one.
- Unit tests: 179 passed, 1 pre-existing xfail.
- Playwright: the full suite (67 tests) passes, including #249's matplotlib fill and re-render cleanup tests, which exercise the registry's `setupFill` cleanup wiring.
